main_body: A bare, gnarled dead tree: a thick trunk with a flared base and several bare branches. No canopy and no horizontal top surface.
top_band: none; the column scan at x=24 shows only outline and branch bark tones (rows 0-10 are branch fragments, 21-62 trunk), with no lighter horizontal surface
evidence: This is an organic tree drawn as a vertical silhouette: trunk and branches with no flat top. The 3/4 top-and-front structure of a built object does not apply to a bare tree, and it is not a column or pillar. The trunk base has a dark plinth-like flare at the bottom with no visible top surface. Judged strictly on the contract, nothing reads as a top band above a front face, so it fails. The kind label 'organic' fits a tree.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. It uses about 3 brown steps (highlight #594736, mid #33281f, outline #16110f). 93% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is near-black, where the references carry tinted outlines (0% neutral). The bark has some banding but no grain, clumps or per-form shading. It is far shallower than the lush, richly textured reference trees and reads as a flat sticker-like silhouette.
